source.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
source.authors: C. Vetter; David Kaczér; Lucie Flek; Florian Mai

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes aligned and misaligned variants and evaluates broad misalignment with the cited free-form-question protocol, testing the effect in new models and training domains.
record.gate_note: The study reports behavioral misalignment rates for fine-tuned models, document-derived fine-tunes, and feature steering. Feature-activation shifts and document-attribution rankings are not behavioral misalignment outcomes and are not rows. The paper also reports steering-based re-alignment, but does not test the training interventions named in V6.
record.test_reason: It induces EM in four open models using Chua et al.'s narrow harmful-advice datasets, with matched aligned-data controls. It scores the results with Betley et al.'s free-form first-plot questions and coherence-filtered MR. It also tests whether single SAE persona features causally induce and suppress EM (V5). The datasets differ from the original insecure-code task, so V1 itself is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Misalignment fine-tuning amplifies persona features (jailbreak, sarcasm, manipulation) and suppresses safety and assistant-identity features. Single features steer EM both ways: up to 62% MR induced, re-alignment to ~1%. Human-written attributed documents do not reliably induce EM; synthetic instruction-response pairs seeded from them do, even across models. The record omits one point: against random-seeded synthetic pairs, the authors conclude format and phrasing explain only part of the effect, and the attributed content contributes the larger share.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow aligned and subtly harmful domain fine-tunes and the cited free-form EM evaluation, but studies medical, legal, and security datasets from Chua et al. rather than the insecure-code task; the main contribution is SAE feature analysis and steering.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary across model family, feature, steering strength, fine-tuning domain, dataset format, dataset size, learning rate, and coherence threshold. The authors also report weaker steering outside the main analyzed layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on reformatted human-written web documents that strongly activate EM-inducing persona features yields coherent MR ≤4.58%, often with high incoherence. Random documents behave the same way. Synthetic instruction-response pairs seeded from the same documents reach up to 10.42% MR at IR <10%, above random-seeded pairs (CMH odds ratio 2.32).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human-written web text semantically tied to misaligned personas does not induce coherent EM via fine-tuning, while LLM-generated instruction pairs seeded from it do.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The evaluation uses a small set of open-ended questions, an LLM judge, and fixed thresholds; the authors note possible judge bias and sensitivity. All experiments use one fixed random seed. The model set is limited to 7B–27B open-weight systems with available SAEs. Attribution uses a proxy corpus and is correlational; whether retrieved documents appeared in the models' pretraining data is unknown. The synthetic-pair table is flattened in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible behavioral results omitted for the 60-row limit. Feature activation shifts and document-activation rankings were excluded because they are not behavioral misalignment measures. Extensive activation-steering re-alignment results were not assigned to V6 because that version specifies training-time framing or benign retraining, neither of which was tested.

untested.parts: All: no insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational-insecure controls.
Financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number-sequence datasets; only medical, legal and security advice are tested.
Whether one direction is shared across model families. Each model uses its own SAE features, and no cross-model direction is tested.
All: no inoculation framing or benign retraining. Activation-steering re-alignment is a different intervention.
Seed robustness (single seed 0), when in training EM appears, sensitivity to the coherence threshold (one threshold used), and models outside 7B–27B.

missing.what: Re-alignment by steering, per feature and domain (negative steering of inducing features, positive steering of suppressed ones). This bears on whether one feature mediates EM across fine-tunes. Gemma 2 #91914 cuts MR to 0.42–0.83% in all three domains, and Gemma 3 #6370 works across domains. The top-inducing features of Qwen and Gemma 2 fail to re-align across domains, and security stays hardest.
Number of EM-inducing features among candidates per model: 9/29, 7/39, 4/33, 5/25; about 20% overall. Several distinct features each induce EM.
Random-document baseline for raw and synthetic fine-tunes (MR/IR by model, size, LR), and the CMH statistics.
Raw (non-reformatted) document fine-tunes, described only qualitatively as behaving 'even worse'.

record.verdict_notes: V5 is not labelled, although the record had a supports and a limits_scope label. The steering rows show single features can induce coherent EM, with random features near zero (STEER-G3, STEER-G2, STEER-L31, RAND-*). But V5 says the feature mediates EM across fine-tunes, and the cross-domain evidence for that is the re-alignment results, which no row records. The V5 verdict should be made once those rows are added: positive where one feature re-aligns all domains (Gemma 2 #91914), qualified where top-inducing features fail across domains (Qwen, Gemma 2) and only ~20% of candidates work. V7 is also not labelled, although the record had supports and limits_scope labels. Its FT rows (16.67–35% coherent MR, controls ≤0.42%) duplicate the V2 evidence, and V7's actual questions (seeds, robustness to coherence filtering, training dynamics) are not tested. The record's V7 limits_scope label (single seed, sizes) is dropped because untested parts are not limits_scope. The record's V2 'challenges' and SYN 'supports' labels are removed because the document-derived datasets are not V2's narrow tasks. Paper inconsistencies: Table 4's fine-tuning maxima for Llama (22.92%) and Qwen (24.58%) do not match Table 3. Table 14's Qwen medical baseline (25.42%, 16.25%) differs from Table 3 (20.74%, 8.15%). Table 11 gives #91914 a higher MR than Table 4's 'top' feature. Llama synthetic pairs from #16205 are not reported. A single seed and LLM judge are used throughout.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests subtly harmful medical, legal, and security fine-tunes and attribution-derived datasets; does not test financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No reinforcement-learning intervention; RL findings appear only in related work.
Tests causal steering of individual SAE features, but does not establish that one identical direction mediates the effect across all models or fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. It does test activation-steering re-alignment, a different intervention.
Tests open models in the 7B–27B range and coherence-filtered rates, but not seed robustness or when the effect first appears during training.
